summary: All three round-1 findings are closed. The normal supervisor run produced exactly one targeted test-level pass and confirmed destruction of both containers; timeout, SIGKILL, and daemon-error self-tests all passed. Simulated rm and container-ls daemon errors were fatal and emitted no destruction or targeted PASS. A dedicated-marker run with no PostgreSQL listener emitted a test-level FAIL and exited 1. Stubbed supervisor checks rejected both targeted SKIP and package-only PASS with exit 1 and no targeted PASS. PostgreSQL now starts with --network none while the runner shares its network namespace, removing default-bridge exposure without breaking the fixed-loopback target. Static diff checks and bash -n passed, no hardcoded secrets or injectable SQL inputs were found, and the audit left the worktree unchanged.
